input.question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?
input.ground_truth: The kidneys and eyes have a higher concentration of capillaries than other organs. High sugar levels in the blood cause capillary damage, thus the two are affected more. Here is an article from [_URL_3_](_URL_0_) and one from another [Reddit post](_URL_1_) in [r/diabetes](_URL_2_). Retino = eyes, Nephro = kidney, -pathy = denoting disorder in a part of the body. & #x200B; Hope that helps. & #x200B; R

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a house, and your blood is like the water that flows through the pipes. When you have type 2 diabetes (DM type 2), the sugar in your blood is too much, like if you put too much sugar in your juice.

Now, your kidneys are like the water filters in your house, and your eyes are like the windows that let you see. Too much sugar in the blood can make the filters in your kidneys get sticky and not work so well over time. That’s why your kidneys can get hurt and that’s called nephropathy.

For your eyes, too much sugar can make the windows cloudy or blurry, so you can’t see as well. That’s called retinopathy.

Other parts of your body can also get affected, but the kidneys and eyes are very sensitive to sugar, so they get hurt first and the most. That’s why doctors pay special attention to them when someone has diabetes.
